Lead, steel and soft iron

Traditional shot is lead. Lead is heavy, so a pellet keeps its speed and energy well; it is also soft, so it is gentle on barrels and chokes. The FITASC rules for Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting are written for lead. They allow at most 28 g of lead shot (up to 2% more is tolerated), in round pellets of one size, 2.0 to 2.5 mm across (±0.1 mm).

But lead is toxic to the environment, especially to waterbirds and water. So more and more grounds and countries restrict it, and the rules change often. Before you travel, check the law of the country and the rules of the ground.

Steel shot is the most common lead-free replacement. A steel pellet is about 30% lighter than a lead pellet of the same size and much harder. So it loses speed sooner and ricochets more from hard surfaces.

Because of ricochets, grounds that allow steel often limit its size, for example to 2.5 mm, and sometimes the cartridge velocity too. Each ground sets its own limits: read the rules posted at the club or ask the organiser.

Soft iron shot is a lead-free shot that is softer than ordinary steel, made to be kinder to barrels and chokes. Bismuth and tungsten alloys are more expensive options: they are heavier than steel and behave more like lead.

Steel pellets need a protective plastic or special wad, so that the hard steel does not scratch the barrel. Some makers offer steel clay loads with biodegradable or fibre wads; check what your ground allows. Which chokes suit steel: Steel shot and chokes.

Where lead shot is already banned or restricted, as of October 2026. Laws change, so check the current text before you travel.

European Union: since 15 February 2023, no shot with 1% lead or more in wetlands or within 100 m of them. The EU is also preparing a wider ban on lead shot away from water. An EU committee approved it in June 2026; once it becomes law, there will be several years before it applies, so check the current state before you travel.

Great Britain: the sale and use of lead shot will be banned for most outdoor shooting from 1 April 2029, including clay shooting. A limited exemption is planned for Olympic and Paralympic athletes.

Denmark: lead shot may not be carried or used for hunting or for clay shooting, including at ranges.

Netherlands: lead shot is banned for hunting, and the national hunters' association states that it is also banned at clay ranges.

Germany: there is no country-wide ban on lead for clay shooting. Three things decide what you may use: the EU rule near water, the hunting law of the federal state (table below) and the ground's own operating permit. So one ground may require steel while the next one does not allow it.

In a 2023 survey by the German Hunting Association, only about half of shotgun shooters said that they could practise with lead-free shot at all.

USA: only non-toxic shot has been allowed for waterfowl hunting since 1991, and some states go further.

Germany by state: lead shot

EU Regulation 2021/57 (REACH, since 15 Feb 2023) applies everywhere in Germany: firing lead shot in wetlands or within 100 m of them is banned, as is carrying it while hunting in wetlands. The state rules below concern hunting (mostly waterfowl or near water), not clay shooting; ranges follow the terms of their own permits. Wording is our summary; only the official text is legally binding. (2026-10)

France: lead shot

As across the EU, Regulation 2021/57 (REACH, since 15 Feb 2023) applies: no firing lead shot in wetlands or within 100 m of them. French hunting law refers to that rule directly, so a breach is also a hunting offence. We found no separate national lead rule for clay ranges; ranges follow the terms of their own permits. In June 2026 the REACH Committee approved a wider restriction on lead in hunting and sport-shooting ammunition with a transition period; as of October 2026 it is not yet in force. Wording is our summary; only the official text is legally binding. (2026-10)

WhereRuleWhat appliesSince
NationalArrêté du 1er août 1986 relatif à divers procédés de chasse (mod. arrêté du 28 décembre 2023), Art. 1 ↗Using lead shot for hunting is banned under the conditions of the EU rule (REACH Annex XVII, entry 63, paras 11–14), i.e. in wetlands and within 100 m of them. Before that, France had its own ban on lead shot in wetlands from 1 June 2006.2023-12-31
NationalArrêté du 1er août 1986 relatif à divers procédés de chasse, Art. 4 ↗Hunting cartridges may not contain lead shot larger than 4 mm or non-lead shot larger than 4.8 mm in diameter.2023-12-31

Italy: lead shot

As across the EU, Regulation 2021/57 (REACH, since 15 Feb 2023) applies: no firing lead shot in wetlands or within 100 m of them. The national rule for Natura 2000 sites goes further on distance (150 m from the shore); regions implement it through their own acts, so details may vary. We found no separate national lead rule for clay ranges. In June 2026 the REACH Committee approved a wider restriction on lead in hunting and sport-shooting ammunition with a transition period; as of October 2026 it is not yet in force. Wording is our summary; only the official text is legally binding. (2026-10)

Spain: lead shot

As across the EU, Regulation 2021/57 (REACH, since 15 Feb 2023) applies: no firing lead shot in wetlands or within 100 m of them. Spain's national rules matter for clay shooting too: they expressly cover sport shooting, so a range in such a zone cannot use lead shot. Hunting is a matter for the autonomous communities; two whose official texts we checked are listed below, others may have their own rules. In June 2026 the REACH Committee approved a wider restriction on lead in hunting and sport-shooting ammunition with a transition period; as of October 2026 it is not yet in force. Wording is our summary; only the official text is legally binding. (2026-10)

Tip: Besides the law, many grounds allow steel shot only, for example to protect the nature around them. That is the ground's own rule, and it applies even where the law allows lead.

Key points

  • The FITASC rules are written for lead shot.
  • EU: no lead shot in wetlands or within 100 m of them since 2023.
  • Steel is lighter and harder than lead, and ricochets more.
  • Grounds often limit the size of steel shot, for example to 2.5 mm.
  • Check the law of the country and the rules of the ground before each trip.

Did you know?

Lead has a density of about 11.3 g/cm³, steel about 7.8–7.9 g/cm³. So a steel pellet of the same diameter is roughly 30% lighter than a lead one.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. Why do grounds often limit the size of steel shot?

    1. Steel is more expensive
    2. Hard steel ricochets more
    3. Large shot does not fit in the hull
    4. FITASC requires it
    Answer

    Hard steel ricochets more

    Hard steel pellets bounce more off hard surfaces, so grounds set limits on size and velocity.

  2. What has applied in the EU since 2023 regarding lead shot?

    1. A complete ban at all grounds
    2. Nothing has changed since 2020
    3. A ban in wetlands and within 100 m of them
    4. Allowed only at FITASC competitions
    Answer

    A ban in wetlands and within 100 m of them

    The EU rule bans lead shot in wetlands and within 100 m of them; some countries have stricter rules.

  3. How does steel shot differ from lead?

    1. It is lighter and harder
    2. It is heavier and softer
    3. There is no real difference
    4. It comes only in small sizes
    Answer

    It is lighter and harder

    Steel is about 30% lighter than lead for the same size and much harder.
